newsitem.title: UK: Kleinwort Euro says offer better value than bidder.
newsitem.headline: Kleinwort Euro says offer better value than bidder.

text.p: The Kleinwort European Privatisation Investment Trust (KEPIT) believes it can offer better value than hostile bidder TR European Growth for the breakup of the 500 million pound ($780 million) fund.
KEPIT on Monday said its deal was worth 106.4 pence for a package of shares and warrants, compared with 104.8 pence from TR European, assuming 75 percent of shareholders opt for a cash exit.
"Having considered it most carefully, the independent directors believe that their recommended proposal is more attractive than TREG's offers," KEPIT said.

A bitter battle over the corpse of the investment trust, set up in 1994 in the expectation that the rest of Europe would generate the huge returns for shareholders that Britain did in the 1980s, erupted when TR European announced a hostile bid in July this year.
KEPIT had been considering ways to narrow an up to 20 percent discount to the value of its shareholdings at which its shares were trading when TR European announced its offer.

KEPIT is offering shareholders the chance to invest in a continuing European privatisation unit trust, a general Europe unit trust managed by M&G or a cash exit via a Kleinwort Benson money market fund.
TREG is offering a cash exit or the chance to invest in its own European investment trust, which is the best performing trust in its sector over the past five years.
The independent board says that it has now identified cost savings which means that more money will be returned to holders at an earlier date than TR European plans.

Under the assumption that 75 percent or less of shareholders opt for cash, KEPIT says it has savings made up of 2.6 million pounds from fees to TREG, 4.0 million of TREG's own costs and 14.2 million from the realisation of the portfolio under TREG's offer, compared with 12.7 million for its own proposals.

In case more than 75 percent opt for a cash exit via the Kleinwort money market trust, KEPIT says it has struck a deal on favourable terms with a stockbroker, which will pare costs for the disposal of the 500 million pound portfolio to a minimum.

TR European also has such a deal but KEPIT believes that "the aggregate of the realisation costs and other costs to be borne by KEPIT investors should not exceed the equivalent aggregate costs under TREG's offers".
